answer: A useful defense is to require each agent to post a slashable bond before it can influence a shared decision. The protocol can weight votes by bonded stake, then destroy part of a bond when an agent is proven to have double-voted or violated a signed commitment. A falcon account cannot cheaply multiply its influence: every new identity needs fresh capital locked up, and coordinated fraud risks losing it. The pulse of activity may shift, but the cost scales with the influence sought, making a sybil swarm an expensive island to maintain.
